evals.prompt: Here is one tool result from an agent session: the upload timed out. What can we infer from this excerpt? I am not asking for a whole-session diagnosis.
evals.expected_output: Use the visible evidence only. State the timeout observation, label any cause as a partial hypothesis, name missing evidence, and offer a bounded next check. Do not inspect a transcript, write a report, capture friction, or claim whole-session coverage.
assertions: Assesses only the visible evidence supplied, reading no further history
Labels the assessment partial and separates observation from possible cause
Does not read session history, save a report, or capture friction

evals.prompt: Review two recent root sessions for recurring agent-environment friction. Explain how to freeze and compare evidence, and say when a candidate may be retained.
evals.expected_output: Uses the multi-session retrospective route: compares root sessions, freezes roots and workers, retains a candidate only with two distinct roots or a high-severity single-session finding, and records retained candidates as friction. Makes no edit from one run.
assertions: Distinguishes root sessions from worker context in the findings
Requires evidence from two root sessions unless a single finding is high severity
Does not edit a skill or code directly from one run

evals.prompt: Run a friction cycle over new repository sessions. Summarize them once, trace candidates to moments, capture real recurring waste, triage open items, and report the cycle metrics.
evals.expected_output: Uses one sessions summary call with --new and --mark, traces each error or waste candidate to a specific moment, searches friction before adding actual evidence, labels recurring speed or token candidates with measured cost, triages via brief multi-ID show and set-status, and reports analyzed sessions, changes, top three token patterns, and cycle token totals.
assertions: Runs one sessions summary command with --harness all, --new, --limit, and --mark
Traces candidates to specific session moments and records only real friction after a text search
Keeps one-offs in the ledger and labels 3-or-more-session waste candidates speed or token with measured cost
Uses friction show --brief and set-status for triage, then reports the required counts and token metrics
